solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dr Tippen is tailored such a suit

indicators.note: a tailor cuts and refits cloth, so the letters of the words before it are cut and refitted into a new order

parts.note: taken letter by letter as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A doctor called Tippen is having a suit made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' is the anagram signal for the ten letters of DR TIPPEN IS. The definition 'such a suit' points back at the whole clue: the suit the doctor is having made is this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit cut from cloth with thin vertical lines is named after that striped pattern, the classic City banker's look.

definitions.meaning: to keep something separate from others, cut off
a stiff is a corpse, and late means dead, so a corpse might own up in the first person that it is so: late

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical, flagged by the question mark: split the answer as I, SO, LATE and it is what a dead body might admit.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine or cut off is to keep apart from others, exactly what setting apart means.

definitions.meaning: an angry outburst in public, as in 'make a fuss'
a play's act is divided into shorter sections set in one place

explanation.surface: A child's tantrum is all part of the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a public fuss is 'making a scene', and a stage act subdivides into those shorter units.

parts.note: a breather is a short pause or rest
room means space, as in 'room to move'

explanation.surface: A place to catch one's breath, set aside for someone called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is American slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: John is US slang for a lavatory, and the polite American word for a public lavatory is this.

clue.text: Deferral for Costa Rica Wine Society

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
CR is the international code for Costa Rica
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
a nation is a society of people under one state

explanation.surface: Putting things off seems to be the motto of a Costa Rican wine club.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitually putting tasks off till later is deferral, a synonym for delaying.

definitions.meaning: Astaire was a famous Hollywood hoofer, an example of someone who performs steps
one of Santa's reindeer, all of whom pull the sleigh behind Rudolph, the red-nosed leader

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire follows the great Rudolph Nureyev onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rudolph' suggests Nureyev, the ballet star, but the second sense is Santa's reindeer team, which Rudolph leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Astaire was a celebrated hoofer, and one of Santa's reindeer in the Christmas poem bears that name too.

parts.note: a pal is a friend
read as the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter

explanation.surface: A friend arrives with their sweetheart, looking rather wan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover but is read as the heart of SWEET, its central E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wan has lost colour from the face, which is a synonym for looking ashen.

clue.text: According to the late Fred Astaire, say

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per the rules'
the late president is the former one, so late means previous

explanation.surface: A quotation attributed to the late Fred Astaire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the late' looks like a reference to Astaire being dead, but it means previous, giving FORMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Astaire was an entertainer on stage and screen, an example of an artiste.

clue.text: Perhaps, islander Sappho harassed Balinese no end

indicators.note: harassed means agitated and troubled, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
the last letter of Balinese is dropped, the word left without its end

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An islander, perhaps the poet Sappho, harassed a Balinese person endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the final E of BALINESE, and 'harassed' rearranges BALINES. 'Perhaps' marks Sappho as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was a poet of Lesbos, so she was a native of that Greek island, perhaps also in the modern sense.

definitions.meaning: the past tense of bide, to wait, as in 'bided their time'
to foretell, as in 'it augurs well'

explanation.definitionFit: It is an old past tense of bide, meaning stayed or waited, and also a verb meaning to portend or presage.

clue.text: "Three cheers for our queer old dean!", à la Oxford don

definitions.text: "Three cheers for our queer old dean!", à la Oxford don

parts.words: "Three cheers for our queer old dean!", à la Oxford don
parts.note: the toast swaps the opening sounds of 'dear old queen', the kind of slip famously attributed to an Oxford don, the Reverend William Spooner

explanation.surface: A toast to an eccentric college head, in the manner of an Oxford academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is said to be a toast to Queen Victoria, 'our dear old queen', with the first sounds swapped; Spooner was warden of New College, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The slip of transposing initial sounds of words is named after the Oxford don William Spooner.
As a verb it means to hurtle along at speed; as a noun it means one's profession or life's work.

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter a is removed from the fodder's letters
spouting suggests words gushing out in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a priestly ruler, taken as written as the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who isn't a priestly ruler is nonetheless spouting pompous language.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of HIEROCRAT ('Not a') and rearrange what is left ('spouting').
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is grandiose, inflated language meant to impress, a pejorative sense of the art of persuasive speech.

indicators.note: struggles suggests twisting and writhing about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter by letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician grapples with someone's urges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with a capital looks like the party, but here it means free-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean lavish or open-handed in giving, a synonym for bountiful.

parts.note: not a concert conductor who is sure of themselves, but an electrical terminal, which may be the anode (positive) or the cathode (negative)

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a confident orchestral conductor; the sense is electrical conduction.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit, and the anode is the positive one.

definitions.meaning: The pseudonym of a Financial Times crossword compiler
a member of a religious order of brothers

explanation.definitionFit: It is the pseudonym of a fellow FT compiler, and a friar or brother belongs to a religious order.

clue.text: Ineffective for one redcap round shelter

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
a redcap is a British military police officer, abbreviated MP
O is round in shape
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: A military policeman circling a shelter proves useless.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcap is British slang for a military police officer, from the red cap worn on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerless and lacking force, so ineffective is a synonym in its general sense.

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for a revolutionary hero.
explanation.definitionFit: To hanker is to long or yearn, as in 'my heart longs for home'.

indicators.note: in places the word for previously inside the abbreviation for California

parts.note: once means formerly, previously

explanation.surface: Something formerly kept in California is to be hidden away.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to keep it out of sight, a direct synonym.

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a human being is one who must die

explanation.surface: A declaration: 'God, I am only human!'
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an exclamation, but 'God' is the definition: a deity cannot die.
explanation.definitionFit: A deity lives forever, so a god is one who never dies.

parts.note: AB stands for able seaman

indicators.note: rearrange means the letters of scene are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor is required to reorganise the stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Need' looks like a verb but is the noun: a lack or want. 'to' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or want of something, as in 'in the absence of food', is a need.

indicators.note: a confiscated item is held by others, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Reuben ignored the fact that his sweet had been confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'Reuben' and the start of 'ignored'. 'Sweet' is the adjective, not a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and gentle in nature, so sweet in the sense of mild and kindly.

clue.text: Three articles on mother's object of loathing

parts.note: the English articles an, a and the, one after another
ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: Three articles written about a mother that she hates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the articles before MA in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or utterly detested is called this, as in 'the idea was to him a thing he loathed'.

clue.text: Love to hum with first player

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
hum is slang for a bad smell, and BO is body odour
1ST, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A musician loves to hum along with the first player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' is British slang for a stink, giving BO (body odour).
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the oboe, a woodwind instrument, is a musician in an orchestra.

definitions.meaning: the initials N and P are November and Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet, and the code word for O falls between them

explanation.surface: Both David Niven and Gregory Peck won Hollywood's top award.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls two actors who each won an Academy Award; the second sense uses the radio alphabet, where N is November and P is Papa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is nicknamed this, and the same name is the radio code word for the letter O.

clue.text: Not unknown for limey bodies to break up and disband

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for an unknown is removed from the fodder
break up means fall apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken letter by letter as the fodder
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Bodies of British sailors break up and are dispersed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Y ('Not unknown') out of LIMEY BODIES and rearrange the rest ('break up'). 'Limey' is old American slang for a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge troops from service, dissolving a military unit, is to disband it.

clue.text: Staff with walking-stick from Malacca, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a rod or stick carried in the hand
a Malacca is a walking stick made from rattan, named after the Malaysian port

explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a hand-held rod, and a Malacca is a rattan stick of the same sort.

definitions.meaning: smutty or indecent, as in a risque joke
the colour of a clear sky

explanation.definitionFit: Smutty jokes and films are so called, and it is also the colour of the sky.

clue.text: Entrant so riled, at the start, to be ruffled and scratched

indicators.note: ruffled means disordered, so the gathered letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken letter by letter as fodder

indicators.note: only the first letter of riled is used

explanation.surface: An entrant so annoyed at the starting line that they are flustered and pull out of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes R from 'riled'; 'to be ruffled' rearranges ENTRANTSO with it. 'Scratched' means withdrawn from a race before it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or runner scratched before the start never begins the race, the literal sense of the hyphenated term.
